'''''Alisma lanceolatum''''' is a species of [[aquatic plant]] in the [[Alismataceae|water plantain family]] known by the common names '''lanceleaf water plantain''' and '''narrow-leaved water plantain'''.<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> It is widespread across [[Europe]], [[North Africa]] and temperate [[Asia]].<ref name=":1" /> It is naturalized in [[Australia]], [[New Zealand]], [[Oregon]], [[California]] and [[British Columbia]]. It is considered a [[noxious weed]] in some places.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=294813|title=World Checklist of Selected Plant Families: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|website=apps.kew.org|language=en-GB|access-date=2017-01-26}}</ref><ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Alisma%20lanceolatum.png Biota of North America Program]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=222000006|title=Alisma lanceolatum in Flora of China @ efloras.org|website=www.efloras.org|access-date=2017-01-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=222000006|title=Alisma lanceolatum in Flora of North America @ efloras.org|website=www.efloras.org|access-date=2017-01-26}}</ref>

This species is a weed of [[Paddy field|rice fields]] in many areas, including [[New South Wales]] and [[California]].

In [[England]] and [[Wales]] it is occasionally locally found, in [[Ireland]] it is rare, and [[Scotland]] it is very rare.

It is found in mud and in fresh waters.

==Description==
[[File:AlismaLanceolatum2.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Part of an inflorescence and single blossom]]
This is a [[Perennial plant|perennial herb]] growing from a [[caudex]] in the water or mud that typically reaches a height of about 0.7 meters and a spread of 0.25 meters.<ref name=":0" /> It produces lance-shaped [[Leaf|leaves]] 12 to 20 centimeters long and 4 wide on long [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]]; leaves which remain submerged in water are smaller and less prominently veined. The [[inflorescence]] is mostly erect and up to half a meter tall.

It produces a wide array of small pinkish-purple three-petalled [[flower]]s that open in the morning, from June until August.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Irish Wildflowers - Narrow-leaved Water-plantain, Alisma lanceolatum|url=http://www.irishwildflowers.ie/pages/416a.html|access-date=2021-04-22|website=www.irishwildflowers.ie}}</ref> The [[fruit]] is a tiny [[achene]] up to 2 or 3 millimeters long clustered into an aggregate fruit of about 20 units. The [[seed]]s are reddish-brown and about 1.5 millimeters long.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Alisma lanceolatum: Narrow-leaved Water-plantain {{!}} NBN Atlas|url=https://species.nbnatlas.org/species/NBNSYS0000002102|access-date=2021-04-22|website=species.nbnatlas.org}}</ref>

== Cultivation ==
Grows best in water 15-30 centimeters deep in full sun. Suitable for [[Hardiness zone|USDA hardiness zones]] 5–8.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Shoot|title=Alisma lanceolatum Narrow-leaved water plantain Care Plant Varieties & Pruning Advice|url=http://www.shootgardening.co.uk/plant/alisma-lanceolatum|access-date=2021-04-22|website=www.shootgardening.co.uk|language=en}}</ref>

==Similar Species==
The water plantain ''[[Alisma plantago-aquatica]]'' has acute leaf tips not tapering to a stalk.<ref name="The Wild Flower Key">{{cite book |last=Rose |first=Francis|author-link=Francis Rose  |title=The Wild Flower Key |year=2006 |publisher=Frederick Warne & Co|isbn=978-0-7232-5175-0 |pages=483–484}}</ref> The flowers of ''A. plantago-aquatica'' also typically open in the afternoon, and the leaves are wider.<ref name=":2" />
